private_notes.notes_fil:
## [purpose] Layunin

Sa pagtatapos ng maikling araling ito, kaya ng BHW na harapin nang mag-isa ang isang bagong sitwasyon — tukuyin ang pangangailangan, piliin ang tamang katuwang (kasama ang kapwa BHW para sa pang-araw-araw na tanong sa trabaho), at sabihin kung paano niya titiyakin ang lokal na contact at susundan ang resulta — at maipakita ang pagkakaiba ng paglapit sa maling tao at sa tamang tao.

## [time-materials] Oras at kagamitan

- **Oras:** mga 30 minuto sa harapang sesyon (ang bahaging "Pagsasanay at buod" sa plano sa gabay ng subchapter). Mga 5 minuto ang sariling pag-aaral ng aralin.
- **Kagamitan:** manila paper at marker; ang slides ng aralin; ang hub-and-spoke na visual ng apat na ugnayan ng module (`01-apat-na-ugnayan.svg`) para sa buod; dalawang role-play card (Mali at Tama, tingnan sa ibaba).

## [prepare] Paghahanda

- Basahin ang aralin sa Read at Slides para alam mo mismo ang nakita ng BHW.
- Ito ang pangwakas na aralin ng module, kaya silipin ang takeaway ng limang ibang aralin; ipapabuod mo ang mga ito sa grupo.
- Alamin kung may pormal na proseso sa inyong lugar sa pag-file ng ulat ng BHW, at kung sino ang supervisor. Sinasabi ng slide na tiyakin sa supervisor ang opisyal na proseso.
- Ang araling ito ay tungkol sa **pagpili at pagsubaybay sa tamang tao**. Huwag ituro kung paano punan ang anumang report form, at huwag magturo ng kahit ano tungkol sa mismong ubo.

## [opening] Pambungad

Itanong sa grupo: *"Naranasan na ba ninyong hindi alam kung sino talaga ang lalapitan? Ano ang ginawa ninyo?"* Kumuha ng dalawa o tatlong kuwento. Isulat sa manila paper kung kanino sila unang lumapit, at sino pala ang talagang kailangan nila.

## [steps] Mga hakbang

1. **Subukan mo: isa pang sitwasyon (Read "Subukan mo: isa pang sitwasyon", unang slide).** Basahin ang sitwasyon ng bagong-tanggap na BHW na nalilito sa pag-file ng kanyang unang ulat. Ipasagot muna sa grupo bago ipakita ang kasunod: *"Sino ang pinakaangkop na lapitan — hindi ang midwife, hindi rin ang barangay officials?"*
2. **Bakit kapwa BHW.** Idiin ang dahilan ng aralin: hindi dahil mas mababa ang usapin, kundi dahil nasa mas matagal nang kapwa BHW ang karanasan sa pang-araw-araw na detalye ng trabaho. Saka ituro ang huling linya ng slide: sa supervisor tinitiyak ang opisyal na proseso.
3. **Mali kumpara sa tama (Read "Mali kumpara sa tama: paglapit sa tamang tao", ikalawang slide).** Basahin ang bersiyong Mali, saka itanong: *"Ano ang naging kapalit — para sa barangay captain at para sa anak ni Aling Nena?"* Basahin ang bersiyong Tama, saka itanong: *"Kailan pumasok ang barangay officials, at bakit noon lang?"*
4. **Ang tatlong hakbang.** Isulat sa manila paper ang tatlong linya ng slide: tukuyin ang pangangailangan, piliin ang tamang katuwang, tiyakin ang lokal na contact at sundan ang resulta. Suriin ang mga kuwento sa pambungad gamit ang tatlong hakbang na ito.
5. **Self-check.** Ibigay ang check (sino ang makatutulong sa karaniwang tanong tungkol sa pag-file ng ulat) at hayaang mag-usap ang grupo bago ibigay ang sagot.
6. **Buod.** Gamit ang hub-and-spoke na visual, magpasabi sa isang BHW bawat ugnayan, sa isang pangungusap, kung kailan niya ito lalapitan.

## [expected-answers] Inaasahang sagot at paano tumugon

- **"Ang midwife — siya ang humahawak ng ulat namin."** Makatwiran, dahil ang midwife ang nagtatakda ng gawain ng BHW tulad ng pag-uulat. Tanggapin, saka itanong: *"Para sa karaniwang 'paano ko ito pupunan' na tanong, sino ang mas malapit at ilang beses nang nakagawa nito?"* Sa midwife o supervisor ang pormal na proseso.
- **"Nahihiya akong magtanong sa kapwa BHW."** Kilalanin ang damdamin. Gamitin ang salita ng aralin: hindi mas mababa ang usapin; doon lang talaga nakatira ang praktikal na karanasan. Itanong kung sino sa silid ang matutuwang matanong.
- **"Hindi naman masama ang bersiyong Mali — puwede namang ipasa ng kapitan."** Huwag makipagtalo. Itanong: *"Gaano katagal bago nakarating sa midwife ang bata? Kaninong oras ang nagamit sa bagay na hindi niya saklaw?"*

## [misconception] Karaniwang maling akala

**"Hindi 'tamang daan' ang pagtatanong sa kapwa BHW — sa opisyal dapat dinadala ang totoong tanong."** May mga BHW na pakiramdam ay may saysay lang ang tanong kapag dinala sa midwife o opisyal. Sinasabi ng aralin na para sa pang-araw-araw na tanong sa trabaho, ang kapwa BHW na may karanasan ang tamang unang lapitan, at ang supervisor para sa opisyal na proseso. Itama ito nang hindi napapahiya ang sinuman: ipataas ang kamay ng mga matagal nang BHW sa silid na nakatulong na sa bagong BHW sa ulat — makikita ng grupo kung gaano ito kakaraniwan.

## [practice] Gawaing pagsasanay

Pangwakas na role-play nang magkapares. **Round 1 (Mali):** isang BHW ang gaganap na BHW Marites, ang isa si Aling Nena; dinala ni Marites ang ubo diretso sa barangay captain "dahil siya naman ang laging kausap ko." **Round 2 (Tama):** uulitin ng parehong pares ito sa tamang paraan. Pagkatapos ng Round 2, ipapaliwanag ng BHW na gumanap na Marites sa sariling salita: ang pangunahing punto (anong uri ng pangangailangan ito), ang unang hakbang (sino ang unang lalapitan), at ano ang titiyakin niya sa midwife o RHU at susundan. Magpalitan ng papel at ulitin gamit ang sitwasyon ng bagong BHW at ulat mula sa unang slide.

## [answer-key] Susi sa self-check

Iisang tanong ang section check sa Read "Mali kumpara sa tama: paglapit sa tamang tao" at ang check sa ikalawang slide; minsan lang itong tinalakay dito.

- **"Sino ang makatutulong sa karaniwang tanong tungkol sa pag-file ng ulat?"** → **Kapwa BHW na may karanasan, at ang supervisor kung kailangan.** Nasa mas matagal nang kapwa BHW ang praktikal na karanasan sa pang-araw-araw na gawain; sa supervisor naman tinitiyak ang opisyal na proseso.
  - Mali ang *"Walang dapat tanungin"* dahil ang pananatiling nalilito ay nagpapaantala sa ulat at sa serbisyo. Hindi nagtatrabaho nang mag-isa ang BHW — bahagi ng trabaho ang pagtatanong sa tamang tao, hindi kahinaan.

## [observe] Ano ang oobserbahan

Gamitin ang observation indicator ng aralin (naipapaliwanag ang pangunahing punto at angkop na unang hakbang sa sitwasyon, kasama ang dapat tiyakin sa supervisor) habang ginagawa ang role-play:

- **Kaya na:** pagkatapos ng round na Tama, napapangalanan ng BHW ang uri ng pangangailangan, sa tamang tao unang lumalapit, at nasasabi ang titiyakin sa midwife, RHU, o supervisor at kung paano susundan — nang walang untag.
- **Kailangan pa ng practice:** tama ang pagganap ng BHW sa round na Tama pero kailangan pa ng tanong mo bago maipaliwanag kung bakit, o bago masabi ang pagsubaybay.
- **Hindi pa:** hindi angkop ang paliwanag o hakbang — halimbawa, sa nakasanayang tao pa rin unang lumalapit kahit sa round na "Tama," o nangangako kay Aling Nena ng sasakyan bago matiyak ang anuman.

Hiwalay ang pag-obserba nito sa silid sa pagtatapos ng BHW sa online self-check. Hindi patunay ng kasanayan ang tamang sagot sa self-check.

## [support] Kung kailangan ng dagdag na suporta

- Ibigay sa isang card ang tatlong hakbang ng slide — tukuyin ang pangangailangan, piliin ang tamang katuwang, tiyakin at sundan — at ipasabi nang malakas ang bawat hakbang habang nagro-role-play.
- Hayaan muna silang gumanap na Aling Nena at panoorin ang kapares na **Kaya na** bilang Marites, saka magpalitan.
- Obserbahan muli gamit ang parehong dalawang sitwasyon sa susunod na sesyon, hindi bago.

## [sources-review] Sanggunian at tala sa pagrepaso

- BHW Reference Manual PDF 15 (source ng aralin, may markang "inherited page reference; final audit pending"). Ayon sa README ng source material, ang "Ang BHW at ang Kanyang Barangay" ay nasa Reference Manual pp. 7–8 (PDF 15–16), Facilitator Guide p. 19 (PDF 26), at Day 1 presentation slides 29–44.
- Galing sa gabay ng subchapter ang pangwakas na role-play na Mali/Tama at ang tanong sa pambungad (script hakbang 8 at mga tanong para sa talakayan). Ang sitwasyon ni Aling Nena at ng bagong BHW ay sariling paraan ng pagtuturo ng aralin, hindi teksto ng source.
- Oras: pinananatili ng module ang 3 oras ng TESDA para sa *Work in a Team Environment* (sinasabi ng Facilitator Guide PDF 26–27 na "at least 3 hours", kasama ang paksang "Pagganap ng Tungkulin bilang Miyembro ng Team"). Ang 30 minuto sa itaas ay bahagi ng araling ito sa planong iyon. Huwag idagdag muli ang buong oras sa bawat maikling aralin; ang hating ito ay para sa self-study, hindi bagong training-hour allocation.
- Pangkalahatan ang observation indicator ng araling ito; mas tiyak ang katumbas na indicator sa mga indicator ng kakayahan ng subchapter para sa pagpili ng tamang ugnayan. Maaaring pagtugmain ito ng mga reviewer.
- Draft na gabay sa talakayan ang `practice-map` na visual ng aralin, hindi pa aprubado ng may-ari.
- Repasuhin ang kasalukuyang legal/policy wording, bilingual parity, at observation indicator bago ilathala.
- Draft para sa pagrepaso (Draft for review)
private_notes.notes_en:
## [purpose] Purpose

By the end of this short lesson the BHW can work through a new situation on their own — identify the need, choose the right partner (including a fellow BHW for everyday work questions), and say how they will confirm the local contact and follow up — and can show the difference between approaching the wrong person and the right one.

## [time-materials] Time and materials

- **Time:** about 30 minutes in a face-to-face session (the "Exercise and summary" part of the plan in the subchapter guide). Self-study of the lesson alone takes about 5 minutes.
- **Materials:** manila paper and markers; the lesson's slides; the module's hub-and-spoke visual of the four relationships (`01-apat-na-ugnayan.svg`) for the summary; two role-play cards (Wrong and Right, see below).

## [prepare] Prepare

- Read the lesson in both Read and Slides so you know exactly what the BHW has seen.
- This lesson closes the module, so skim the other five lessons' takeaways; you will ask the group to summarize them.
- Know whether your area has a formal procedure for filing BHW reports, and who the supervisor is. The slide says to confirm formal procedures with the supervisor.
- This lesson is about **choosing and following up with the right person**. Do not teach how to fill in any report form, and do not teach anything about the cough itself.

## [opening] Opening

Ask the group: *"Has it happened to you that you weren't sure who to actually approach? What did you do?"* Take two or three stories. Write on manila paper who they went to first, and who they ended up needing.

## [steps] Steps

1. **Try it: one more situation (Read "Try it: one more situation", first slide).** Read the situation about the newly accredited BHW who is confused about filing their first report. Ask the group to answer before you show the rest: *"Who is the most fitting person to approach — not the midwife, not barangay officials?"*
2. **Why a fellow BHW.** Stress the lesson's reason: not because it is a lesser concern, but because the everyday, practical know-how of the work lives with experienced fellow BHWs. Then point to the slide's last line: formal procedures are confirmed with the supervisor.
3. **Wrong versus right (Read "Wrong versus right: approaching the right person", second slide).** Read the Wrong version, then ask: *"What did it cost — for the barangay captain and for Aling Nena's child?"* Read the Right version, then ask: *"When did barangay officials come in, and why only then?"*
4. **The three steps.** Put the slide's three lines on manila paper: identify the need, choose the right partner, confirm the local contact and follow up on the result. Check the stories from the opening against these three steps.
5. **Self-check.** Give the check (who can help with an ordinary question about filing a report) and let the group discuss before revealing the answer.
6. **Summary.** Using the hub-and-spoke visual, ask one BHW per relationship to say, in one sentence, when they would approach it.

## [expected-answers] Expected answers and how to respond

- **"The midwife — she handles our reports."** Reasonable, since the midwife sets BHWs' tasks such as reporting. Accept it, then ask: *"For an ordinary 'how do I fill this in' question, who is closer and has done it many times?"* Keep the midwife/supervisor for formal procedures.
- **"I'd be embarrassed to ask another BHW."** Acknowledge the feeling. Use the lesson's words: it is not a lesser concern; that is simply where the practical know-how lives. Ask who in the room would be glad to be asked.
- **"The Wrong version isn't so bad — the captain can pass it on."** Do not argue. Ask: *"How much time passed before the child reached the midwife? Whose time was used on something outside their role?"*

## [misconception] Common misconception

**"Asking a fellow BHW is not the 'proper' channel — real questions should go to officials."** Some BHWs feel a question only counts if it goes up to the midwife or an official. The lesson says that for everyday work questions an experienced fellow BHW is the right first contact, with the supervisor for formal procedures. Correct it without embarrassing anyone: ask the experienced BHWs in the room to raise their hands if they have helped a new BHW with a report — let the group see how normal it is.

## [practice] Practice activity

Closing role-play in pairs. **Round 1 (Wrong):** one BHW plays BHW Marites, the other plays Aling Nena; Marites takes the cough straight to the barangay captain "because he's the one I usually talk to." **Round 2 (Right):** the same pair replays it the right way. After Round 2, the BHW playing Marites explains in their own words: the main point (what kind of need this is), the first action (who she approaches first), and what she would confirm with the midwife or RHU and follow up on. Swap roles and repeat with the new-BHW report situation from the first slide.

## [answer-key] Self-check answer key

The section check in Read "Wrong versus right: approaching the right person" and the check on the second slide are the same question; it is covered once here.

- **"Who can help with an ordinary question about filing a report?"** → **An experienced fellow BHW, and the supervisor when needed.** Everyday, practical know-how of the work lives with experienced fellow BHWs; formal procedures are confirmed with the supervisor.
  - *"Nobody should be asked"* is wrong because staying stuck delays the report and the service. A BHW never works alone — asking the right person is part of the work, not a weakness.

## [observe] What to observe

Use the lesson's observation indicator (explains the main point and an appropriate first action, including what must be checked with the supervisor) during the role-play:

- **Kaya na:** after the Right round, the BHW names the kind of need, approaches the right person first, and says what to confirm with the midwife, RHU or supervisor and how they will follow up — without prompting.
- **Kailangan pa ng practice:** the BHW plays the Right round correctly but needs your follow-up question to explain why, or to name the follow-up step.
- **Hindi pa:** the explanation or action does not fit — for example, the "Right" round still goes to the usual person first, or the BHW promises Aling Nena transport before anything is confirmed.

Observing this in the room is separate from the BHW finishing the online self-check. A correct self-check answer is not evidence of the skill.

## [support] If a BHW needs more support

- Give them the slide's three steps on a card — identify the need, choose the right partner, confirm and follow up — and ask them to say each step out loud during the role-play.
- Let them play Aling Nena first and watch a partner rated **Kaya na** play Marites, then swap.
- Re-observe with the same two situations at the next session, not new ones.

- BHW Reference Manual PDF 15 (lesson source, marked "inherited page reference; final audit pending"). The source-material README maps "Ang BHW at ang Kanyang Barangay" to Reference Manual pp. 7–8 (PDF 15–16), Facilitator Guide p. 19 (PDF 26) and Day 1 presentation slides 29–44.
- The Wrong/Right closing role-play and the opening question come from the subchapter guide (script step 8 and discussion prompts). The Aling Nena and new-BHW situations are the lesson's own teaching devices, not source text.
- Timing: the module keeps TESDA's 3 hours for *Work in a Team Environment* (Facilitator Guide PDF 26–27 says "at least 3 hours", shared with the "Pagganap ng Tungkulin bilang Miyembro ng Team" topic). The 30 minutes above is this lesson's share of that plan. Do not repeat the whole allocation for each short lesson; this split supports self-study and does not create a new training-hour allocation.
- This lesson's observation indicator is generic; the subchapter's competency indicators include a more specific indicator for choosing the right relationship. Reviewers may want to align them.
- The lesson's `practice-map` visual is a draft discussion guide, not owner-approved.
- Review current legal/policy wording, bilingual parity and the observation indicator before publication.

objectives_en: Explain and apply in a situation: the accreditation process.

read_sections.body_en: Demi prepares a question about registration and accreditation. ‘Who reviews an application, and how can I verify the official decision?’ This is a fictional situation; we have not established that Demi has an application, registration or accreditation. RA 7883 places accreditation with the local health board under DOH guidelines. Registration and accreditation are related but distinct steps. Asking a question, attending training or holding a title does not prove that the process is complete.
read_sections.body_fil: Naghahanda si Demi ng tanong tungkol sa rehistrasyon at akreditasyon. ‘Sino ang tumitingin sa aplikasyon, at saan ko makikita ang opisyal na tala ng pasya?’ Kathang-isip ang sitwasyong ito; hindi pa natin alam kung may aplikasyon, rehistrasyon o akreditasyon si Demi. Sa RA 7883, nakaugnay ang akreditasyon sa local health board, ayon sa gabay ng DOH. Magkaugnay ngunit magkaibang hakbang ang rehistrasyon at akreditasyon. Ang pagtatanong, pagdalo sa pagsasanay o pagkakaroon ng titulo ay hindi patunay na tapos na ang proseso.
read_sections.takeaway_en: Understand the roles and verify the decision; do not assume status.
read_sections.takeaway_fil: Unawain ang tungkulin at tiyakin ang pasya; huwag ipagpalagay ang status.

read_sections.body_en: The local health board has specific responsibilities. The joint DILG and DOH circular issued in 2023 lists its duties: safeguard registration and accreditation; evaluate and act on applications; record decisions in a board resolution or meeting minutes; issue certificates to qualified BHWs; review and approve benefits using local funds; recommend benefits and fund allocation; provide a copy of the BHW registry to DOH; and monitor services. An accreditation decision and review of a benefit using local funds are different decisions. The board may also create a BHW Registration and Accreditation Committee. The facilitator guide describes screening, interviews, recommendations to the board and registry preparation as supporting committee tasks. A recommendation alone is not the board’s official decision.
read_sections.body_fil: May tiyak na pananagutan ang local health board. Inililista ng magkasanib na circular ng DILG at DOH noong 2023 ang mga tungkulin nito: pangalagaan ang proseso ng rehistrasyon at akreditasyon; suriin at aksiyunan ang mga aplikasyon; itala ang pasya sa board resolution o minutes ng pulong; maglabas ng sertipiko sa mga kwalipikadong BHW; suriin at aprubahan ang mga benepisyong gagamit ng pondong lokal; magrekomenda ng benepisyo at paglalaan ng pondo; magbigay ng kopya ng BHW registry sa DOH; at magsagawa ng monitoring sa serbisyo. Magkahiwalay ang pasya sa akreditasyon at ang pagsusuri ng benepisyong may lokal na pondo. Maaari ring bumuo ang board ng BHW Registration and Accreditation Committee. Inilalarawan ng facilitator guide ang pagsusuri, panayam, rekomendasyon sa board at pag-aayos ng registry bilang mga tungkuling pantulong ng komite. Ang rekomendasyon lamang ng komite ay hindi katumbas ng opisyal na pasya ng board.
read_sections.takeaway_en: The board is responsible; the committee assists and decisions have official records.
read_sections.takeaway_fil: May pananagutan ang board; pantulong ang komite at may opisyal na tala ang pasya.

read_sections.body_en: Compare the two roles. A committee helps screen applications and recommend action; the board is responsible for acting and officially recording its decision. The circular encourages municipal and city health boards to create a committee. If none exists yet or creation is pending, the board remains responsible for facilitating registration and accreditation. Find out the actual local arrangement rather than assume every locality has the same committee and office. The RHU or municipal or city health office can help identify the proper contact. Their assistance, an interview or a training certificate does not replace an official decision.
read_sections.body_fil: Ihambing ang dalawang papel. Tumutulong ang komite sa pagsusuri at rekomendasyon; pananagutan ng board ang pag-aksiyon at opisyal na pagtatala ng pasya. Hinihikayat ng circular ang mga municipal at city health board na bumuo ng komite. Kapag wala pa nito o habang binubuo ito, nananatili sa board ang tungkuling padaliin ang rehistrasyon at akreditasyon. Kaya dapat alamin ang aktuwal na lokal na ayos, sa halip na ipagpalagay na pare-pareho ang komite at opisina sa lahat ng lugar. Makapagtuturo ng tamang contact ang RHU o municipal o city health office. Hindi kapalit ng opisyal na pasya ang kanilang tulong, isang panayam o isang training certificate.
read_sections.takeaway_en: Verify who assists and where the board’s decision is recorded.
read_sections.takeaway_fil: Tiyakin kung sino ang tumutulong at saan nakatala ang pasya ng board.

read_sections.body_en: Demi uses three fictional practice cards. A has only a training certificate; it does not prove accreditation. B has a committee recommendation but no verified board decision. C mentions a board resolution, but its process, scope and verification contact remain unclear. None of the cards decides a person’s status. Match each known fact to the missing information: what is the next step for A, is there an official decision for B, and which official record should be checked for C? Do not invent a local form, fee, deadline or result.
read_sections.body_fil: Tatlong kathang-isip na practice card ang ginagamit ni Demi. Sa A, may training certificate lamang; hindi nito pinatutunayan ang akreditasyon. Sa B, may rekomendasyon ng komite ngunit walang natiyak na pasya ng board. Sa C, may binanggit na board resolution ngunit hindi pa natiyak kung para sa anong proseso, sino ang saklaw at saan ito makukumpirma. Walang card na nagpapasya sa status ng tao. Itapat ang bawat alam na detalye sa kulang na impormasyon: anong susunod na hakbang sa A, may opisyal na pasya na ba sa B, at aling opisyal na tala ang dapat tiyakin sa C? Huwag mag-imbento ng lokal na form, bayad, deadline o resulta.
read_sections.takeaway_en: Separate known facts from what needs verification; do not guess approval.
read_sections.takeaway_fil: Ihiwalay ang alam na detalye sa kailangang tiyakin; walang hulang approval.

read_sections.body_en: Demi chooses Card B. On a blank planning sheet, she writes: ‘For this example with a committee recommendation, which office can confirm whether the local health board has made an official decision, where can it be verified, and what is the next step if none has been made?’ The question names the process, known fact, missing information and proper contact. Ask the locally confirmed RHU, municipal or city health office, or board contact for current guidance. This practice submits no actual application or private documents. Proof of registration, proof of accreditation and a training certificate should not be treated as interchangeable.
read_sections.body_fil: Pinili ni Demi ang Card B. Sa blankong planning sheet, isinulat niya: ‘Para sa halimbawang may rekomendasyon ng komite, aling tanggapan ang makapagsasabi kung may opisyal na pasya na ang local health board, saan ito matitiyak, at ano ang susunod na hakbang kung wala pa?’ Tiyak ang tanong: pangalan ng proseso, alam na detalye, kulang na impormasyon at tamang contact. Makipag-ugnayan sa locally confirmed na RHU, municipal o city health office, o board contact para sa kasalukuyang gabay. Walang tunay na aplikasyon o pribadong dokumentong isusumite sa pagsasanay. Ang katibayan ng rehistrasyon, katibayan ng akreditasyon at training certificate ay hindi dapat ipagpalit sa isa’t isa.
read_sections.takeaway_en: Connect the question to the process, known fact and official record.
read_sections.takeaway_fil: Iugnay ang tanong sa proseso, alam na detalye at opisyal na tala.

options.en: The recommendation is a supporting step. Ask the proper local contact whether the board has decided, where it can be verified and what comes next.
options.fil: Pantulong ang rekomendasyon. Tiyakin sa tamang lokal na contact kung may pasya na ang board, saan ito makukumpirma at ano ang susunod na hakbang.

options.en: The committee recommendation automatically grants accreditation; the board’s decision or record need not be checked.
options.fil: Automatic nang accredited dahil nagrekomenda ang komite; hindi na kailangang tiyakin ang pasya o tala ng board.

options.en: A training certificate, BHWE or job title is enough to replace registration and accreditation.
options.fil: Sapat na ang training certificate, BHWE o job title bilang kapalit ng rehistrasyon at akreditasyon.

check.prompt_en: Card B has a committee recommendation but no verified official decision. What is Demi’s best explanation and next question?
check.prompt_fil: Sa Card B, may rekomendasyon ng komite ngunit walang natiyak na opisyal na pasya. Ano ang pinakamainam na paliwanag at susunod na tanong ni Demi?
check.feedback_en: First: correct. A committee recommendation and the local health board’s official decision are different. The decision and record remain unverified in the card; the question addresses the missing information and next step without asserting status. Second: incorrect. Screening or recommendation alone is not automatic approval. It does not establish that the board acted, recorded a decision or issued the appropriate certificate. Third: incorrect. Training certificates, BHWE, job titles, registration and accreditation serve different purposes. Those labels or credentials cannot replace the accreditation process or establish the card’s official decision. Completing the online lesson does not grant accreditation either.
check.feedback_fil: Una: tama. Magkaiba ang rekomendasyon ng komite at opisyal na pasya ng local health board. Hindi pa natiyak ang pasya at tala sa card; tinutugunan ng tanong ang kulang na impormasyon at susunod na hakbang nang walang pag-aangkin ng status. Ikalawa: mali. Hindi automatic approval ang pagsusuri o rekomendasyon lamang. Hindi nito pinatutunayang umaksiyon ang board, nagtala ng pasya o naglabas ng naaangkop na sertipiko. Ikatlo: mali. Magkakaiba ang gamit ng training certificate, BHWE, job title, rehistrasyon at akreditasyon. Hindi kapalit ng accreditation process ang mga label o credential na iyon at hindi nila pinatutunayan ang opisyal na pasya sa card. Hindi rin nagbibigay ng akreditasyon ang online lesson completion.

read_sections.body_en: Return to Card B: there is a committee recommendation, but no verified official decision. What should Demi explain? Distinguish the recommendation from the board’s decision, name the missing information, and choose a question about the process and official record. A training certificate, BHWE or job title does not replace accreditation. Choose an answer, then read the reasons for all options. Completing the online lesson is separate from observed competency and does not grant accreditation.
read_sections.body_fil: Balikan ang Card B: may rekomendasyon ng komite, ngunit wala pang natiyak na opisyal na pasya. Ano ang dapat ipaliwanag ni Demi? Ihiwalay ang rekomendasyon sa pasya ng board, sabihin ang kulang na impormasyon, at pumili ng tanong na magpapalinaw sa proseso at opisyal na tala. Hindi ipinapalit ang training certificate, Barangay Health Worker Eligibility o job title sa akreditasyon. Piliin ang sagot, saka basahin ang dahilan para sa lahat ng pagpipilian. Ang pagkumpleto sa online lesson ay hiwalay sa obserbasyon ng kasanayan at hindi nagbibigay ng akreditasyon.
read_sections.takeaway_en: Explain the roles, identify the gap and verify the official decision.
read_sections.takeaway_fil: Ipaliwanag ang mga papel, tukuyin ang kulang at tiyakin ang opisyal na pasya.

private_notes.notes_fil:
## [purpose] Layunin

Suportahan ang iisang layunin ng lesson: maipaliwanag at mailapat sa isang sitwasyon ang proseso ng akreditasyon. Ihiwalay ang pananagutan ng local health board sa tulong ng komite, tukuyin ang alam at kulang na impormasyon, at bumuo ng tiyak na tanong tungkol sa proseso at opisyal na tala ng pasya. Huwag magpasya sa eligibility o accreditation status ng learner. Kathang-isip at authored practice si Demi at Cards A–C; hindi sila halimbawa mula sa source o tunay na pasya ng board.

## [time-materials] Oras at kagamitan

Panatilihin ang kasalukuyang 30-minutong bahagi ng lesson sa 180-minutong module. Authored teaching split: pagbubukas 3 minuto; papel at tala 8; fictional cards 6; pagsasanay sa tanong 5; application check 5; suportadong re-practice 3. Hiwalay dito ang optional story at replays. Authored estimate ang 8–10 minuto para sa sariling pag-aaral: humigit-kumulang 6 minuto ang anim na encoded Read narration, dagdag ang 2–4 minuto para sa pag-iisip at lahat ng application rationales. Hindi kasama ang optional story at audio replays; hindi ito TESDA accreditation requirement.

Gamitin ang anim na screen, blankong papel, tatlong malinaw na fictional cards, role cards at source sheet. Sa role cards: “komite: suriin, kapanayamin, magrekomenda, tumulong sa registry” at “board: aksiyunan, itala ang pasya, maglabas ng sertipiko sa kwalipikadong BHW.” Huwag humingi ng tunay na sertipiko, personal na service record, accreditation status o pinunang aplikasyon. Gamit sa talakayan ang blankong folder sa illustration.

## [prepare] Paghahanda

Basahin ang source audit at tiyakin ang kasalukuyang lokal na gabay sa tamang tanggapan bago mag-facilitate. Alamin ang locally confirmed na RHU, municipal/city health office o board contact; huwag mag-imbento ng opisina, delegated authority, form, bayad, deadline, registry platform o certificate format. Ipaliwanag na batas ang RA 7883, pambansang administrative guidance ang nilagdaang DILG–DOH circular, training summary ang facilitator guide, at para sa kani-kanilang LGU ang mga lokal na order. Hindi pa natiyak sa audit na ito ang buong national IRR at amendment history.

Ihanda ang Cards A–C gamit lamang ang nakasaad na kathang detalye. A: training certificate lamang. B: rekomendasyon ng komite, walang natiyak na pasya ng board. C: may binanggit na resolution, ngunit hindi alam ang proseso, saklaw at verification contact. Blangko ang lahat ng personal na field. Maaaring magsalita, sumulat o tumuro sa role cards ang learner.

## [opening] Pagbubukas

Ipakita ang bagong clinic scene ni Demi. Itanong: “Sino ang tumitingin sa aplikasyon, at paano matitiyak ang opisyal na pasya?” Tanggapin ang kawalan ng katiyakan bilang simula ng mabuting tanong. Hindi patunay ng kumpletong rehistrasyon o akreditasyon ang pagtatanong, pagdalo sa training o pagkakaroon ng titulo. Walang kailangang magbahagi ng personal na status. Basahin ang layunin sa napiling wika ng learner.

## [steps] Mga hakbang

1. Gamitin ang pinanatiling section-5 screen upang ipaliwanag ang walong nakalistang tungkulin ng board. Igrupo bilang proseso/pasya/tala, sertipiko/registry/pagmamanman, at benepisyo/pondo. Authored teaching aid ang paggrupong ito. Magkaibang pasya ang akreditasyon at pagsusuri ng benepisyong gagamit ng lokal na pondo.
2. Ihambing ang role cards ng komite at board. Maaaring bumuo ng komite ang board; hinihikayat ito ng circular. Kapag wala pa o habang binubuo, pinadadali pa rin ng board ang rehistrasyon/akreditasyon. Hindi patunay ng opisyal na pasya ang rekomendasyon lamang.
3. I-model ang Card A: ebidensiya ng training ang alam; kulang ang aktuwal na registration/accreditation process at susunod na hakbang. Magtanong sa locally confirmed na tanggapan. Huwag mangako ng resulta.
4. Ipahambing sa magkapareha ang B at C. Tukuyin ang isang alam, isang kulang at isang tiyak na verification question.
5. I-model ang tanong ni Demi para sa B. Ipaliwanag muna ang pagkakaiba ng papel bago itanong ang opisyal na pasya, tala at susunod na hakbang.
6. Sagutan ang three-choice check, talakayin ang lahat ng dahilan at magbigay ng ibang fictional card para sa re-practice. Pantulong at hiwalay sa completion ang optional story.

## [expected-answers] Inaasahang paliwanag

Pananagutan ng local health board ang pag-aksiyon sa aplikasyon at pagtatala ng pasya. Kung may komite, tumutulong ito sa pagsusuri, panayam, rekomendasyon at registry. Kailangang tiyakin ang tamang lokal na ayos. Hindi automatic approval ang rekomendasyon. Magkakaiba ang gamit ng training, registration at accreditation evidence. Hindi kapalit ng akreditasyon ang BHWE o job title. Kung may binanggit na resolution sa hindi pa natiyak na card, itanong ang proseso at saklaw; huwag hulaan ang status ng tao.

Tinutukoy ng kapaki-pakinabang na sagot ang proseso, alam na detalye, kulang na impormasyon at tamang local contact. Hindi kailangang isaulo ang lahat ng walong tungkulin; kailangang maipaliwanag at mailapat nang tama ang pagkakaiba ng papel at tala.

## [misconception] Maling akala at puna

“May rekomendasyon ng komite, kaya automatic na accredited.” Sabihin: “May mahalagang hakbang kang napansin. Hindi pa natiyak ang opisyal na pasya ng board. Aling tala at tanggapan ang makapagpapalinaw?”

“Kapalit ng proseso ang training certificate o job title.” Sabihin: “Maaaring mahalaga ang detalyeng iyon, ngunit iba ito sa patunay ng rehistrasyon o akreditasyon. Pangalanan natin ang kulang na hakbang nang walang pangakong approval.”

Huwag ipahiya ang learner dahil may hindi pa alam. Huwag gawing personal na assessment, legal ruling o tunay na application instruction ang fictional card.

## [practice] Kathang role at process cards

Gumamit ng blankong sheet na may apat na column: alam na detalye / may tungkulin / kulang na impormasyon / tiyak na tanong. Worked Card A: “training certificate / proseso ng board, gabay ng health office / susunod na registration o accreditation step / aling tanggapan ang magtitiyak ng kasalukuyang proseso at ebidensiya?”

Worked Card B: “rekomendasyon ng komite / tumutulong ang komite, umaaksiyon ang board / opisyal na pasya at tala / aling tanggapan ang magtitiyak kung may pasya, saan ito makukumpirma at ano ang susunod?”

Worked Card C: “may binanggit na resolution / tala ng board, authorized local contact / proseso at saklaw / aling opisyal na tala ang magtitiyak sa naging pasya at kung sino ang saklaw?” Hindi patunay ng approval o refusal ang pagbanggit lamang. Walang tunay na record na hinihingi.

Magpalitan ng papel: magpaliwanag ang isa, magtanong tungkol sa kulang ang isa. Palitan ang card at ulitin. Manatiling fictional ang nakasulat na output; observation level at maikling puna lamang ang itala.

## [answer-key] Application check at mga dahilan

Tama ang Choice 1: magkaiba ang rekomendasyon ng komite at opisyal na pasya ng board. Hindi pa natiyak ang pasya at tala sa card; tinutugunan ng tiyak na lokal na tanong ang kulang at susunod na hakbang nang walang pag-aangkin ng status.

Mali ang Choice 2: hindi automatic approval ang pagsusuri o rekomendasyon lamang. Hindi nito pinatutunayang umaksiyon ang board, nagtala ng pasya o naglabas ng naaangkop na sertipiko.

Mali ang Choice 3: hindi kapalit ng rehistrasyon/akreditasyon ang training certificate, BHWE o job title. Magkakaiba ang gamit ng mga ito at hindi nila pinatutunayan ang opisyal na pasya o status sa card. Hindi rin nagbibigay ng akreditasyon ang online lesson completion.

Pagkatapos ng anumang sagot, ipaliwanag ang tamang pagkakaiba at ipabago ang isang tanong. Ibigay ang buong katumbas na Filipino o English rationale, kasama ang dahilan sa mga hindi piniling option.

## [observe] Obserbahan at itala

Gamitin ang iisang indicator na nakaayon sa lesson objective. Obserbahan ang paliwanag sa papel ng board/komite, paghiwalay ng alam na detalye sa kulang na pasya/tala, at pagbuo ng bounded process question. Gamitin ang tatlong antas sa napiling wika: kaya na, kailangan ng practice o hindi pa. Paliwanag at paglalapat ang tasahin, hindi tunay na credential, accent, bilis sa pagbasa o pribadong status.

Hiwalay ang online completion sa observed competency. Hindi sapat na ebidensiya ng sariling paliwanag ang tamang pagpili lamang. Maaaring sumangguni sa source sheet; itala ang kailangang untag at magbigay ng isang konkretong susunod na pagsasanay.

## [support] Suporta at re-practice

Sentence frames: “Maaaring tumulong ang komite sa __; pananagutan ng board ang __.” “Nakasaad sa card ang __; kailangan pang tiyakin ang __.” “Aling locally confirmed na tanggapan ang makapagpapalinaw sa __ at susunod na hakbang?”

Kung kailangan ng suporta sa pagbasa, basahin ang card at hayaang tumuro sa role cards ang learner. Para sa kumpiyansa, i-model ang isang sagot, ipapaliwanag sa kapareha, saka gumamit ng ibang fictional card sa re-practice. Tiyak na puna: “Naihiwalay mo ang rekomendasyon sa pasya. Pangalanan naman ang tala o contact na dapat tiyakin.” Walang sapilitang personal na pagbabahagi sa grupo.

## [sources-review] Mga source at limitasyon

Sinusuportahan ng seksiyon 3–4 at 7 ng RA 7883 ang accreditation authority, registration/proof at local-fund review. Sinusuportahan ng opisyal na nilagdaang DILG–DOH JMC No. 2023-001, 24 Agosto 2023, PDF 2–7/printed 2–7, ang gabay sa pagbuo ng komite, tungkulin ng board at tulong ng municipal/city health office. Buod ng board/committee duties ang original 126-page Drive facilitator guide PDF 25/printed 18; PDF 27/printed 18 ang katumbas sa 150-page TCI version. Independiyenteng nasuri ang aktuwal na mga page image at offset. Hindi buong IRR ang guide. Pinagtitibay ng opisyal na Roxas at Marilao orders ang committee tasks sa kani-kanilang LGU lamang.

Tatlong oras para sa buong competency ang rekomendasyon sa original guide PDF 23/printed 16. Sa opisyal na TESDA Barangay Health Services NC II Revision 01, promulgated 11 Enero 2019, unit 400311213, PDF 19–20/printed 15–16 at PDF 86–87/printed 82–83, may tig-iisang oras ang tatlong outcome. Wala sa mga ito ang hiwalay na TESDA 30-minute accreditation requirement; panatilihin ang kasalukuyang course allocation.

Fresh source audit: 5 Oktubre 2026. Hindi pa natiyak ang buong national IRR, kumpletong amendment/enactment history, circular publication/ONAR filing at target local procedure. Tiyakin ang kasalukuyang lokal na gabay bago mag-facilitate. Draft ang content, bagong art, narration at stories; kailangan pa ng hiwalay na 1.4.4 owner approval. Hindi patunay ng human listening o independent policy SME review ang model-mediated media inspection. Walang pahintulot na i-merge, i-deploy sa production o i-publish ang draft na ito.
private_notes.notes_en:
## [purpose] Purpose

Support the lesson’s single objective: explain and apply the accreditation process in a situation. Learners distinguish local health board responsibilities from committee assistance, separate known facts from missing information, and form a specific question about the process and official decision record. Do not determine any learner’s eligibility or accreditation status. Fictional Demi and Cards A–C are authored practice, not cases from a source or actual board decisions.

## [time-materials] Time and materials

Retain the existing 30-minute lesson share within the 180-minute module. Authored teaching split: opening 3 minutes; roles and records 8; fictional cards 6; question practice 5; application check 5; supportive re-practice 3. Optional story and replays are outside this split. Measure self-study against the completed encoded narration before final packaging; it is an authored estimate, not a TESDA accreditation requirement.

Use the six lesson screens, blank paper, three clearly fictional cards, role cards and a source sheet. Role cards read “committee: screen, interview, recommend, help maintain registry” and “board: act, record decision, issue certificates to qualified BHWs.” Never request real certificates, personal service records, accreditation status or a completed application. The digital illustration’s blank folder is a discussion prop.

## [prepare] Prepare

Read the source audit and confirm current local guidance with the responsible office before facilitation. Know the locally confirmed RHU, municipal/city health office or board contact; do not invent an office, delegation, form, fee, deadline, registry platform or certificate format. Explain that RA 7883 is the statute, the signed DILG–DOH circular is national administrative guidance, the facilitator guide is a training summary, and specific LGU orders apply in their respective localities. Complete national IRR and amendment history remain unverified in this audit.

Prepare Cards A–C using only the stated fictional facts. A: training certificate only. B: committee recommendation, no verified board decision. C: a resolution is mentioned, but its process, scope and verification contact are unknown. Leave all personal fields blank. Allow speaking, writing or pointing to the role cards.

## [opening] Opening

Show Demi’s new clinic scene. Ask: “Who reviews an application, and how could an official decision be verified?” Accept uncertainty as a useful starting point. State that asking, attending training or holding a title does not establish completion of registration or accreditation. No personal status disclosure is expected. Read the objective in the learner’s chosen language.

## [steps] Steps

1. Use the preserved section-5 screen to explain the board’s eight listed duties. Group them as process/decision/record, certificates/registry/monitoring, and benefits/funding. Grouping is an authored teaching aid. Benefit review using local funds and an accreditation decision are separate decisions.
2. Compare committee and board role cards. The board may create a committee; the circular encourages its creation. If absent or pending creation, the board still facilitates registration/accreditation. A committee recommendation alone does not establish an official board decision.
3. Model Card A: the known fact is training evidence; the missing fact is the actual registration/accreditation process and next step. Ask the locally confirmed office. Do not promise a result.
4. Have pairs compare B and C, identifying one known fact, one gap and one specific verification question.
5. Model Demi’s Card B question. Learners explain the role distinction before asking about the official decision, record and next step.
6. Complete the three-choice check, discuss all reasons and offer another fictional card for re-practice. Optional story supports learning but is independent of completion.

## [expected-answers] Expected explanations

The local health board has responsibility for acting on applications and recording decisions. A committee, where created, assists with screening, interviews, recommendations and registry work. The proper local arrangement needs confirmation. A recommendation is not automatic approval. Training, registration and accreditation evidence have different purposes. BHWE and job titles do not substitute for accreditation. A resolution mentioned in an unverified card requires checking its process and scope, not guessing a person’s status.

A useful response names the process, known fact, missing information and appropriate local contact. Learners need not recite all eight duties; they must explain the role/record distinction and apply it accurately.

## [misconception] Misconception and feedback

“The committee recommended it, so accreditation is automatic.” Say: “You noticed a relevant step. What remains unverified is the board’s official decision. Which record and office could clarify that?”

“A training certificate or job title replaces the process.” Say: “That fact may be relevant, but it is different from proof of registration or accreditation. Let us name the missing step without promising approval.”

Do not shame a learner for uncertainty. Do not turn a fictional card into a personal assessment, legal ruling or actual application instruction.

## [practice] Fictional role and process cards

Use a four-column blank sheet: known fact / responsible role / missing information / specific question. Worked Card A: “training certificate / local board process, health office guidance / next registration or accreditation step / which office confirms the current process and evidence?”

Worked Card B: “committee recommendation / committee assists, board acts / official decision and record / which office confirms whether the board decided, where it can be verified and what comes next?”

Worked Card C: “resolution mentioned / board record, authorized local contact / process and scope / which official record confirms what decision was made and whom it covers?” A mention alone proves neither approval nor refusal. No actual records are requested.

Partners exchange roles: one explains, the other asks for the missing information. Swap cards and repeat. Keep written output fictional; record only the observation level and brief feedback.

## [answer-key] Application check and reasons

Choice 1 is correct: committee recommendation and official board decision are different. The card leaves the decision and record unverified; the specific local question addresses that gap and the next step without asserting status.

Choice 2 is incorrect: screening or recommendation alone is not automatic approval. It does not establish that the board acted, recorded a decision or issued the appropriate certificate.

Choice 3 is incorrect: a training certificate, BHWE or a job title cannot replace registration/accreditation. These serve different purposes and do not establish the card’s official decision or status. Completing the online lesson also grants no accreditation.

After any choice, ask the learner to explain the correct distinction and revise one question. Provide the full equivalent Filipino or English rationale, including reasons for the unselected options.

## [observe] Observe and record

Use the one indicator aligned to the lesson objective. Observe the learner explaining board/committee roles, distinguishing known facts from a missing decision/record, and forming a bounded process question. Use the three levels in the chosen language: kaya na, kailangan ng practice, or hindi pa. Judge the explanation and application, not a real credential, accent, literacy speed or private status.

Online completion is separate from observed competency. Correctly selecting an option alone is insufficient evidence of an independent explanation. A learner may consult the source sheet; record prompts needed and give one concrete next practice step.

## [support] Support and re-practice

Sentence frames: “The committee can help with __; the board is responsible for __.” “The card says __; we still need to verify __.” “Which locally confirmed office can clarify __ and the next step?”

For reading support, read a card aloud and let the learner point to the role cards. For confidence support, model one answer, invite a partner explanation and then re-practise with a different fictional card. Give specific feedback: “You separated the recommendation from the decision. Now name the record or contact to verify.” No forced public disclosure.

## [sources-review] Sources and review limits

RA 7883 sections 3–4 and 7 support accreditation authority, registration/proof and local-fund review. The official signed DILG–DOH JMC No. 2023-001, 24 August 2023, PDF 2–7/printed 2–7, supports committee creation guidance, board duties and municipal/city health office assistance. Original 126-page Drive facilitator guide PDF 25/printed 18 summarizes board/committee duties; the 150-page TCI version’s corresponding page is PDF 27/printed 18. These offsets were independently visually checked. The guide is not the complete IRR. Official Roxas and Marilao orders corroborate committee tasks only within those LGUs.

The original guide’s PDF 23/printed 16 recommends three hours for the whole competency. Official TESDA Barangay Health Services NC II Revision 01, promulgated 11 January 2019, unit 400311213, PDF 19–20/printed 15–16 and PDF 86–87/printed 82–83, independently allocates three one-hour outcomes. Neither establishes a separate TESDA 30-minute accreditation requirement; retain the existing course allocation.

Fresh source audit: 5 October 2026. Full national IRR, exhaustive amendment/enactment history, circular publication/ONAR filing and target local procedure remain unverified. Confirm current local guidance before facilitation. Content, new art, narration and stories are draft pending separate 1.4.4 owner approval. Model-mediated media inspection does not establish human listening or independent policy SME review. No merge, production deployment or publication is authorized for this draft.

levels.kaya_na_en: Accurate roles, known/missing information and a specific question about the official decision/record and next step, without prompts or status claims.
levels.hindi_pa_en: Cannot yet distinguish roles and decisions, decides from a label or recommendation, or cannot identify the gap and appropriate question.
levels.kaya_na_fil: Tamang papel, alam/kulang na impormasyon at tiyak na tanong sa opisyal na pasya/tala at susunod na hakbang, nang walang untag o pag-aangkin ng status.
levels.hindi_pa_fil: Hindi pa naihihiwalay ang papel at pasya, nagpapasya mula sa label o rekomendasyon, o hindi pa matukoy ang kulang at tamang tanong.
levels.kailangan_practice_en: Correct direction but needs prompts to distinguish recommendation from decision, identify the gap or make the local question specific.
levels.kailangan_practice_fil: Tama ang direksiyon ngunit kailangan ng untag upang ihiwalay ang rekomendasyon sa pasya, tukuyin ang kulang o gawing tiyak ang lokal na tanong.

observation_indicators.not_yet_en: Treats a recommendation or credential as automatic approval, cannot identify missing information, or promises accreditation from the card alone.
observation_indicators.not_yet_fil: Itinuturing na automatic approval ang rekomendasyon o credential, hindi natutukoy ang kulang na impormasyon, o nangangako ng akreditasyon mula sa card lamang.
observation_indicators.observable_en: Explains and applies board and committee roles in a fictional situation, separates known facts from a missing decision/record, and forms a specific local process/next-step question without asserting accreditation.
observation_indicators.observable_fil: Naipapaliwanag at nailalapat ang papel ng board at komite sa kathang sitwasyon, naihihiwalay ang alam sa kulang na pasya/tala, at nakabubuo ng tiyak na lokal na tanong tungkol sa proseso at susunod na hakbang nang walang pag-aangkin ng akreditasyon.

objectives_fil: Maipaliwanag at mailapat sa isang sitwasyon: pamamahala sa sarili.
objectives_en: Explain and apply in a situation: managing your own work.

read_sections.body_en:
Because each BHW is still just one person, they also need skills aimed inward — not only skills for relating to others.

Six skills matter: being **reliable** — delivering the good service expected of them; **stress management** — staying calm and focused under pressure; **time management** — prioritizing what matters so work finishes on time; being **trustworthy** — holding to principles and moral standards; **adaptability** — willing to accept and keep up with change; and being **honest and careful** — thoughtful in what is said and how others are treated.
read_sections.body_fil:
Dahil isang tao lang ang bawat BHW, kailangan din niya ng mga kasanayang pang-sarili — hindi lang pang-ugnayan sa iba.

Anim na kasanayan ang dapat taglayin: **maasahan** — makapaghatid ng mabuting serbisyong inaasahan sa kanya; **stress management** — pagiging kalmado at tutok sa trabaho sa kabila ng tensyon; **time management** — kaya niyang unahin ang mas importanteng gawain upang matapos sa takdang oras; **mapagkakatiwalaan** — may prinsipyo at sumusunod sa pamantayang moral; **adaptability** — handang tumanggap at makisabay sa pagbabago; at **matapat at maingat** — maalalahanin sa sinasabi at sa pakikitungo sa ibang tao.
read_sections.takeaway_en: Six self-management skills support a BHW — it isn't only the ability to relate to others that matters, but keeping yourself steady too.
read_sections.takeaway_fil: Anim na kasanayan sa self-management ang sumusuporta sa BHW — hindi lang ang kakayahang makipag-ugnayan sa iba ang kailangan, kundi ang pagpapanatili ng sarili.

options.en: A specific goal, realistic timing and weekly review.
options.fil: Tiyak na layunin, makatotohanang oras, at lingguhang pagrepaso.

read_sections.body_en:
These skills aren't natural to everyone — but there are specific ways to develop them.

Practice self-care, since stress lowers performance. Train yourself to be patient, since everyone has their own timeline. Finish one task at a time, since multitasking doesn't actually get more done. Reflect on your own abilities — you improve faster once you know them. Set specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, time-bound (SMART) goals. Plan each week's work in writing. Come to meetings prepared — ask for the agenda and read materials beforehand. And think before you speak.
read_sections.body_fil:
Hindi likas sa lahat ang mga kasanayang ito — pero may mga tiyak na paraan para mapaunlad ito.

Mag-alaga sa sarili, dahil ang stress ay nagpapababa ng performance. Sanayin ang sariling maging matiyaga, dahil may sariling timeline ang bawat tao. Tapusin ang isang gawain sa isang pagkakataon, dahil hindi nagreresulta sa pagkumpleto ang multitasking. Pagnilayan ang sariling kakayahan — mas mapapabuti mo ito kung kilala mo ito. Magtakda ng mga target na tiyak, nasusukat, naaabot, makatotohanan, at may hangganan sa oras (SMART). Magplano ng bawat linggo ng trabaho, nakasulat. Dumalo sa mga pulong nang handa — hingin ang agenda at basahin ang mga materyales bago pumunta. At mag-isip muna bago magsalita.
read_sections.takeaway_en: Self-management isn't a natural skill — it's developed through specific habits: planning, reflection, and thinking before speaking.
read_sections.takeaway_fil: Ang self-management ay hindi likas na kasanayan — ito ay pinapaunlad sa pamamagitan ng tiyak na ugali: pagpaplano, pagninilay, at pag-iisip bago magsalita.

slides.narration_en:
Because each BHW is still just one person, they also need skills aimed inward — not only skills for relating to others.

Six skills matter: being **reliable** — delivering the good service expected of them; **stress management** — staying calm and focused under pressure; **time management** — prioritizing what matters so work finishes on time; being **trustworthy** — holding to principles and moral standards; **adaptability** — willing to accept and keep up with change; and being **honest and careful** — thoughtful in what is said and how others are treated.
slides.narration_fil:
Dahil isang tao lang ang bawat BHW, kailangan din niya ng mga kasanayang pang-sarili — hindi lang pang-ugnayan sa iba.

Anim na kasanayan ang dapat taglayin: **maasahan** — makapaghatid ng mabuting serbisyong inaasahan sa kanya; **stress management** — pagiging kalmado at tutok sa trabaho sa kabila ng tensyon; **time management** — kaya niyang unahin ang mas importanteng gawain upang matapos sa takdang oras; **mapagkakatiwalaan** — may prinsipyo at sumusunod sa pamantayang moral; **adaptability** — handang tumanggap at makisabay sa pagbabago; at **matapat at maingat** — maalalahanin sa sinasabi at sa pakikitungo sa ibang tao.

## [purpose] Layunin

Sa pagtatapos ng maikling araling ito, kaya ng BHW na pangalanan ang anim na kasanayan sa self-management, masabi kung alin ang kanyang kalakasan at alin ang kailangan pang paunlarin, at makasulat ng isang SMART goal at nakasulat na plano para sa linggo — kasama ang paliwanag sa unang hakbang at kung ano ang titiyakin niya sa midwife.

## [time-materials] Oras at kagamitan

- **Oras:** mga 40 minuto sa harapang sesyon (ang bahaging "Self-management: kasanayan at pagpapaunlad" sa plano sa gabay ng subchapter). Mga 5 minuto ang sariling pag-aaral ng aralin.
- **Kagamitan:** manila paper at marker; ang slides ng aralin; isang papel at ballpen para sa bawat BHW; isang manila paper na nakasulat ang limang salita ng SMART (tiyak, nasusukat, naaabot, makatotohanan, may hangganan sa oras).

## [prepare] Paghahanda

- Basahin ang aralin sa Read at Slides para alam mo mismo ang nakita ng BHW.
- Sumulat ng sarili mong SMART goal mula sa sarili mong gawain bilang halimbawa, at isang malabong goal ("gagaling ako") para paghambingin.
- Ang araling ito ay tungkol sa **mga ugaling nagpapanatiling maayos sa sariling gawain ng BHW**. Huwag magbigay ng payo tungkol sa mental health, sakit, o personal na problema; kung may BHW na magbahagi ng matinding stress, makinig, at kausapin siya nang pribado pagkatapos ng sesyon, hindi sa harap ng grupo.

## [opening] Pambungad

Itanong sa grupo: *"Alalahanin ang pinakaabalang linggo ninyo bilang BHW. Ano ang nakatulong para malampasan ito? Ano ang nagpahirap?"* Isulat ang mga sagot sa dalawang hanay sa manila paper. Huwag munang magkomento — babalikan ninyo ito.

## [steps] Mga hakbang

1. **Mga kasanayan sa self-management (Read "Mga kasanayan sa self-management", unang slide).** Isa-isahin ang anim na kasanayan: maasahan, stress management, time management, mapagkakatiwalaan, adaptability, matapat at maingat. Huwag itong ipakita bilang checklist lang. Itanong sa bawat BHW: *"Alin dito ang pinakamalakas sa inyo? Alin ang kailangan pang paunlarin?"*
2. **Balikan ang pambungad.** Ituro ang hanay na "nagpahirap." Itanong: *"Alin sa anim na kasanayan ang makatutulong dito?"*
3. **Paano pagbutihin ang self-management (Read "Paano pagbutihin ang self-management", ikalawang slide).** Basahin ang listahan ng mga ugali: pag-aalaga sa sarili, pagiging matiyaga, isang gawain sa isang pagkakataon, pagninilay sa sariling kakayahan, SMART goal, nakasulat na lingguhang plano, pagdalo sa pulong nang handa, at pag-iisip bago magsalita. Itanong: *"Alin dito ang kaya mong simulan ngayong linggo?"*
4. **SMART goal.** Ipakita nang magkatabi ang malabo mong goal at ang SMART goal mo sa manila paper ng SMART. Ipaturo sa grupo kung alin sa limang bahagi ang kulang sa malabong goal.
5. **Self-check.** Ibigay ang check (aling plano ang makatutulong sa self-management) at hayaang mag-usap ang grupo bago ibigay ang sagot.

## [expected-answers] Inaasahang sagot at paano tumugon

- **"Hindi lang talaga ako organisado."** Huwag sumagot ng "kaya mo naman." Sa halip, ituro ang ikalawang slide: *"Tungkol sa mga gawi ang listahang ito, hindi sa pagkatao. Aling isang gawi ang puwede mong subukan muna?"*
- **"Wala akong oras mag-alaga sa sarili — kailangan ako ng komunidad."** Kilalanin ang dedikasyon. Gamitin ang dahilan ng aralin: ang stress ay nagpapababa ng performance. Itanong: *"Kapag pagod na pagod ka, ano ang nangyayari sa pagbisita mo sa bahay-bahay?"*
- **"Ang goal ko ay maging mas mabuting BHW."** Tanggapin bilang simula, saka itanong: *"Mas magaling saan? Kailan? Paano mo malalaman?"* Tulungan silang gawin itong SMART goal.

## [misconception] Karaniwang maling akala

**"Ang self-management ay likas na kakayahan — mayroon ka man nito o wala."** Karaniwang akala ito, lalo na sa mga bagong BHW na itinuturing na permanenteng katotohanan ang "hindi talaga ako organisado." Huwag itong itama sa pagsasabing "kaya mo naman." Sa halip, ipakita ang seksyong "Paano pagbutihin ang self-management" bilang patunay na kasanayan ito na pinapaunlad sa pamamagitan ng tiyak na ugali — pagpaplano, pagninilay, at pag-iisip bago magsalita — hindi katangiang taglay mo na o wala.

## [practice] Gawaing pagsasanay

Mag-isang gagawa ang bawat BHW nang 10 minuto at isusulat: (1) isang kasanayan sa self-management na kalakasan niya at isang kailangan pang paunlarin; (2) isang SMART goal na kaugnay ng kasanayang kailangan pang paunlarin; (3) nakasulat na plano para sa mga gawaing BHW sa susunod na linggo, may markang isang prayoridad. Pagkatapos, magkapares, ipapaliwanag ng bawat BHW ang kanyang papel sa sariling salita: ang pangunahing punto (aling kasanayan at bakit), ang unang hakbang na gagawin ngayong linggo, at ano ang titiyakin niya sa midwife (halimbawa, kung tugma ang mga prayoridad niya sa mga gawaing itinakda ng midwife). Maglibot at makinig.

## [answer-key] Susi sa self-check

Iisang tanong ang section check sa Read "Paano pagbutihin ang self-management" at ang check sa ikalawang slide; minsan lang itong tinalakay dito.

- **"Aling plano ang makatutulong sa self-management?"** → **Tiyak na layunin, makatotohanang oras, at lingguhang pagrepaso.** Tugma ito sa mga ugaling itinuturo ng aralin: magtakda ng SMART goal at magplano ng bawat linggo ng trabaho nang nakasulat.
  - Mali ang *"Sabay-sabay na gawin ang lahat nang walang prayoridad"* dahil sinasabi ng aralin na tapusin ang isang gawain sa isang pagkakataon — hindi nagreresulta sa pagkumpleto ang multitasking — at ang time management ay pag-una sa mas importanteng gawain para matapos sa takdang oras.

## [observe] Ano ang oobserbahan

Gamitin ang observation indicator ng aralin (naipapaliwanag ang pangunahing punto at angkop na unang hakbang sa sitwasyon, kasama ang dapat tiyakin sa supervisor) habang ginagawa ang gawaing pagsasanay:

- **Kaya na:** malinaw na naipapaliwanag ng BHW ang napiling kasanayan at SMART goal, may tiyak na unang hakbang ngayong linggo, at nasasabi ang titiyakin sa midwife — nang walang untag.
- **Kailangan pa ng practice:** tama ang direksiyon ng BHW (may goal at plano) pero kailangan pa ng tanong mo sa detalye — halimbawa, walang hangganan sa oras o paraan ng pagsukat ang goal, o hindi pa masabi kung ano ang titiyakin sa midwife.
- **Hindi pa:** hindi angkop ang paliwanag o hakbang — halimbawa, pangkalahatan lang ang goal ("gagaling ako"), walang nakasulat na plano, o hindi masabi ang sariling kalakasan o ang kasanayang paghuhusayan.

Hiwalay ang pag-obserba nito sa silid sa pagtatapos ng BHW sa online self-check. Hindi patunay ng kasanayan ang tamang sagot sa self-check.

## [support] Kung kailangan ng dagdag na suporta

- Umupo kasama nila at sabay na isulat muli ang isang goal, isang salita ng SMART sa bawat pagkakataon; hayaang sila na lang ang sumulat ng ikalawang goal.
- Paliitin ang plano: sa halip na buong linggo, ang susunod na dalawang araw lang, may isang prayoridad.
- Ipadala ang nakasulat nilang lingguhang plano sa susunod na sesyon at obserbahan muli sa pagpapaliwanag nila rito, kasama kung ano ang tiniyak nila sa midwife.

## [sources-review] Sanggunian at tala sa pagrepaso

- BHW Reference Manual PDF 17–18 at PDF 18 (mga source ng aralin, may markang "inherited page reference; final audit pending"). Ayon sa README ng source material, ang Team Work + Self-Management ay nasa Reference Manual pp. 9–10 (PDF 17–18), Facilitator Guide p. 20 (PDF 27), at Day 1 presentation slides 47–55. Inirerekomenda ng Facilitator Guide PDF 27 na iugnay ang mga kasanayan sa self-management sa dating karanasan ng mga BHW sa kanilang komunidad.
- Hindi pagkakatugma sa lugar ng paksa: inilalagay ng competency table ang self-management sa *Work in a Team Environment*; inililista naman ito ng Facilitator's Manual p. 16 (PDF 23) sa *Develop life and career decisions*. Sinusunod ng module ang competency table.
- Oras: pinananatili ng module ang 3 oras ng TESDA para sa *Work in a Team Environment* (sinasabi ng Facilitator Guide PDF 26–27 na "at least 3 hours"). Ang 40 minuto sa itaas ay bahagi ng araling ito sa planong iyon. Huwag idagdag muli ang buong oras sa bawat maikling aralin; ang hating ito ay para sa self-study, hindi bagong training-hour allocation.
- Galing sa gabay ng subchapter ang naipangalanang maling akala at ang pagsulat ng SMART goal.
- Pangkalahatan ang observation indicator ng araling ito; mas tiyak ang indicator para sa layuning ito sa mga indicator ng kakayahan ng subchapter (pagsulat ng SMART goal at lingguhang plano, at pagtukoy ng kalakasan at kasanayang paghuhusayan). Maaaring pagtugmain ito ng mga reviewer.
- Draft na gabay sa talakayan ang `practice-map` na visual ng aralin, hindi pa aprubado ng may-ari.
- Repasuhin ang kasalukuyang legal/policy wording, bilingual parity, at observation indicator bago ilathala.
- Draft para sa pagrepaso (Draft for review)
private_notes.notes_en:
## [purpose] Purpose

By the end of this short lesson the BHW can name the six self-management skills, say which is their strength and which needs work, and write one SMART goal and a written plan for the week — explaining the first step and what they would check with the midwife.

## [time-materials] Time and materials

- **Time:** about 40 minutes in a face-to-face session (the "Self-management: skills and how to develop them" part of the plan in the subchapter guide). Self-study of the lesson alone takes about 5 minutes.
- **Materials:** manila paper and markers; the lesson's slides; a sheet of paper and a pen for each BHW; a manila paper with the five SMART words written out (specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, time-bound).

## [prepare] Prepare

- Read the lesson in both Read and Slides so you know exactly what the BHW has seen.
- Write one SMART goal of your own from your own work as an example, and one vague goal ("I'll get better") to contrast it with.
- This lesson is about **habits that keep the BHW's own work on track**. Do not give advice on mental health, illness or personal problems; if a BHW shares serious stress, listen, and talk with them privately after the session rather than in front of the group.

## [opening] Opening

Ask the group: *"Think of your busiest week as a BHW. What helped you get through it? What made it harder?"* Write the answers in two columns on manila paper. Do not comment yet — you will come back to them.

## [steps] Steps

1. **Self-management skills (Read "Self-management skills", first slide).** Go through the six skills: reliable, stress management, time management, trustworthy, adaptability, honest and careful. Do not present them as a checklist. Ask each BHW: *"Which of these is already your strength? Which needs work?"*
2. **Back to the opening.** Point to the "made it harder" column. Ask: *"Which of the six skills would have helped here?"*
3. **How to improve self-management (Read "How to improve self-management", second slide).** Read the list of habits: self-care, patience, one task at a time, reflecting on your own abilities, SMART goals, a written weekly plan, coming to meetings prepared, thinking before speaking. Ask: *"Which one could you start this week?"*
4. **SMART goals.** Show your vague goal and your SMART goal side by side on the SMART manila paper. Ask the group to point out which of the five parts the vague goal is missing.
5. **Self-check.** Give the check (which plan supports self-management) and let the group discuss before revealing the answer.

## [expected-answers] Expected answers and how to respond

- **"I'm just not an organized person."** Do not reply with "of course you can." Point to the second slide instead: *"This list is about habits, not personality. Which one habit could you try first?"*
- **"I don't have time for self-care — the community needs me."** Acknowledge the dedication. Use the lesson's reason: stress lowers performance. Ask: *"When you are exhausted, what happens to your house visits?"*
- **"My goal is to be a better BHW."** Accept it as a starting point, then ask: *"Better at what? By when? How will you know?"* Help them turn it into a SMART goal.

## [misconception] Common misconception

**"Self-management is a natural ability — either you have it or you don't."** This is common, especially among new BHWs who take "I'm just not an organized person" as a permanent truth. Don't correct it by saying "of course you can do it." Instead, show the "How to improve self-management" section as proof that this is a skill developed through specific habits — planning, reflection and thinking before speaking — not a trait you either have or lack.

## [practice] Practice activity

Each BHW works alone for 10 minutes and writes: (1) one self-management skill that is their strength and one that needs work; (2) one SMART goal linked to the skill that needs work; (3) a written plan for next week's BHW tasks with one priority marked. Then, in pairs, each BHW explains their page in their own words: the main point (which skill and why), the first step they will take this week, and what they would check with the midwife (for example, whether their week's priorities match the tasks the midwife has set). Walk around and listen.

## [answer-key] Self-check answer key

The section check in Read "How to improve self-management" and the check on the second slide are the same question; it is covered once here.

- **"Which plan supports self-management?"** → **A specific goal, realistic timing and weekly review.** This matches the lesson's habits: set SMART goals and plan each week's work in writing.
  - *"Do everything at once without priorities"* is wrong because the lesson says to finish one task at a time — multitasking doesn't actually get more done — and time management means prioritizing what matters so work finishes on time.

## [observe] What to observe

Use the lesson's observation indicator (explains the main point and an appropriate first action, including what must be checked with the supervisor) during the practice activity:

- **Kaya na:** the BHW explains their skill choice and SMART goal clearly, names a concrete first step for this week, and says what they would check with the midwife — without prompting.
- **Kailangan pa ng practice:** the BHW has the right direction (a goal and a plan) but needs your follow-up question on details — for example, the goal is missing a time limit or a way to measure it, or they cannot yet say what to check with the midwife.
- **Hindi pa:** the explanation or action does not fit — for example, the goal is only general ("I'll get better"), there is no written plan, or the BHW cannot name a strength or a skill to work on.

Observing this in the room is separate from the BHW finishing the online self-check. A correct self-check answer is not evidence of the skill.

## [support] If a BHW needs more support

- Sit with them and rewrite one goal together, one SMART word at a time; let them write the second goal alone.
- Narrow the plan: instead of the whole week, plan just the next two days with one priority.
- Ask them to bring their written weekly plan to the next session and re-observe by having them explain it, including what they checked with the midwife.

## [sources-review] Sources and review notes

- BHW Reference Manual PDF 17–18 and PDF 18 (lesson sources, marked "inherited page reference; final audit pending"). The source-material README maps Team Work + Self-Management to Reference Manual pp. 9–10 (PDF 17–18), Facilitator Guide p. 20 (PDF 27) and Day 1 presentation slides 47–55. Facilitator Guide PDF 27 recommends relating the self-management skills to BHWs' previous experiences in their communities.
- Placement discrepancy: the competency table puts self-management under *Work in a Team Environment*; the Facilitator's Manual p. 16 (PDF 23) lists it under *Develop life and career decisions*. The module follows the competency table.
- Timing: the module keeps TESDA's 3 hours for *Work in a Team Environment* (Facilitator Guide PDF 26–27 says "at least 3 hours"). The 40 minutes above is this lesson's share of that plan. Do not repeat the whole allocation for each short lesson; this split supports self-study and does not create a new training-hour allocation.
- The named misconception and the SMART-goal exercise come from the subchapter guide.
- This lesson's observation indicator is generic; the subchapter's competency indicators include a more specific indicator for this objective (writing a SMART goal and weekly plan, naming a strength and a skill to work on). Reviewers may want to align them.
- The lesson's `practice-map` visual is a draft discussion guide, not owner-approved.
- Review current legal/policy wording, bilingual parity and the observation indicator before publication.
- Draft for review

read_sections.body_en:
In the previous lesson, BHW Mimi checked why the lights and fan were on in an empty meeting area. In this fictional continuation, she confirms another activity is scheduled there; she does not simply turn them off. She also learns there is no clear reminder of who checks the schedule after a meeting.

Now she will form one workable suggestion: a small first step with a reason, consistent with local rules and service needs. It is not yet permission to act or a promise of savings. The story is optional; you can complete Read or Slides without watching it.
read_sections.body_fil:
Sa naunang aralin, sinuri ni BHW Mimi ang nakabukas na ilaw at fan sa bakanteng meeting area. Sa pagpapatuloy ng kathang-isip na kuwento, nakumpirma niyang may susunod na gawain doon; hindi niya ito basta pinatay. Napag-alaman ding walang malinaw na paalala kung sino ang titingin sa schedule pagkatapos ng meeting.

Ngayon, bubuo siya ng isang mungkahing maisasagawa: isang maliit na unang hakbang na may dahilan, naaayon sa lokal na tuntunin at hindi nakasasagabal sa serbisyo. Hindi pa ito pahintulot na kumilos o pangakong makatitipid. Opsyonal ang kuwento; maaaring tapusin ang Read o Slides nang hindi nanonood.
read_sections.heading_fil: Mula sa pansin, tungo sa mungkahi
read_sections.takeaway_en: Separate the observation, proposal, checks and follow-up.
read_sections.takeaway_fil: Ihiwalay ang nakita, mungkahi, dapat tiyakin at follow-up.

read_sections.body_en:
Mimi says: “After the meeting, the lights and fan were on in the meeting area. I confirmed another activity was scheduled, but there was no clear reminder of who checks the schedule.” This is the concern to discuss, without accusing anyone of carelessness.

If a record is needed, include the date, time, place and observation using the local process. State what remains unknown, such as an existing checklist or assigned duty. Omit patient data, guesses about motives and savings amounts that have not been measured.
